A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CPO research and contain 27 pages, including appendices A–J. Text, equations, tables and figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on CUB, AwA2 and CelebA, including task accuracy, concept AUC, interventions, noise robustness and additional appendix analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including uncertainty, computational-cost and sequential-CBM evaluations.

M1.justification: The CPO objective, negative-concept sampling, Gumbel-Softmax procedure and prior choices are unchanged. The new discussion of reward-based alternatives concerns future work, not an implemented method revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use CUB, AwA2 and CelebA with the same tasks and scenarios, including concept-label noise, interventions, streaming concept labels and image occlusion.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged across corresponding experiments: BCE-trained CBMs and CEMs, joint and sequential ProbCBMs, and CoopCBM remain in their respective comparisons. Appendix J retains the same sequential-CBM comparison.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A–B retain the same splits, preprocessing, training budgets, hyperparameter searches, metrics, noise levels and intervention procedures. No new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The gradient visualizations, streaming-initialization comparisons, noise robustness tests and qualitative and quantitative uncertainty analyses are retained. Appendices D–H introduce no new ablation, robustness test or case study.

E5.justification: The same plus/minus reporting, error bars and shaded uncertainty bands are retained. Neither version adds run counts, seeds, confidence-interval definitions or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and the empirical figures retain their results. For example, Table 1 reports CBM-CPO CUB task accuracy of 0.800 ± 0.003 in both versions; Appendix J's sequential-CBM results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, CPO derivation, gradient bounds and posterior-approximation reasoning in Sections 3–4 and Appendices C and E are unchanged. The expanded Figure 1 caption adds explanation without revising the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the core claims about concept-posterior optimization, noise robustness, intervention performance and minimal computational overhead. The added code statement and future directions do not redefine the scientific contributions.

C2.justification: New Section 6 explains why the work uses end-to-end differentiability and states that it is not essential, discussing visual-consistency rewards and learned reward functions as future alternatives. Existing interpretations of the experimental results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds a project-specific GitHub code link in the abstract. v2 only points to the upstream CEM repository in Appendix A. Implementation settings and resource descriptions are otherwise unchanged; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work comparisons are unchanged, including positioning against ProbCBMs, SCBMs and preference-optimization methods. The bibliography differs only in formatting and placement.

P1.justification: Section 6 changes from Conclusion to Discussion, adding a Future Work paragraph and retaining the conclusion under a paragraph heading. Limited introduction edits, caption expansion and an additional funding acknowledgment accompany this local restructuring.

P2.justification: Figure 1's caption now identifies the optimal, empirical and learned sampling sources. The code footnote and discussion expansion cause limited page reflow, while all graphical panels and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v4 modestly improves reproducibility documentation through a project-specific code pointer and improves explanation through Figure 1's expanded caption and Section 6's discussion of reward-based alternatives. The scientific evidence, proofs and appendix results remain unchanged, so the overall benefit is limited.
